name: Rudbeckia

project_scope.selection_mode: Asteraceae batch 3 — ragweeds, thistles, and common roadside species

study_strategy.warning: This batch includes several groups where flower color alone is weak; use leaf and involucre characters.

look_here_first: Check leaf attachment and hairs BEFORE the yellow rays: smooth clasping leaves = R. amplexicaulis; coarse hairy nonclasping leaves = R. hirta; giant glaucous basal leaves and mostly bare flowering stems = R. maxima.
shared_genus_traits: Asteraceae heads with ray florets surrounding a raised disk; leafy herbs with an involucre of phyllaries.
Yellow rays and dark disk color overlap; leaf-base structure, pubescence and disk shape separate these species more reliably.

species_comparison_matrix.amplexicaulis: Sessile leaves with rounded clasping bases
species_comparison_matrix.maxima: Huge leaves mainly basal; flowering stalk sparsely leafy

overlap_and_cautions: Do not use yellow rays or a dark disk alone; all three share these features.
Young or sterile plants may lack diagnostic disk shapes; prioritize leaves and inspect several nodes.
R. maxima is a nonlocal comparison where appropriate; do not infer county nativity from inclusion.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.look_for: Sunflower head architecture and phyllaries; confirm genus rather than assuming any yellow-rayed dark-centered head is Rudbeckia.
Deeply dissected foliage differs from broad glaucous basal leaves of R. maxima; confirm source-pool status before making it a canonical card.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Stem node side-by-side with leaf bases
Whole basal rosette plus flowering stem
Disk cone side profiles with scale
diagnostic_photo_checklist.character: Conical, ovoid, and tall elongated disks

handoffs.task: Obtain matched leaf-base, hair, basal-leaf and disk-side views; reuse canonical species images where diagnostic.
